name: memos
description: Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app that brings your everyday thoughts together in a personal timeline. Your data stays yours, and you choose what to keep private or share.

### Seconds to write. Yours to keep. Memos is a place for every quick thought. No title, no folder, nothing to pick: type, and the thought is kept on the day you wrote it. Your memos stay where you decide, yours alone until you share one with family and friends. [Demo](https://demo.usememos.com) · [Install](#quick-start) · [Docs](https://usememos.com/docs) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/tfPJa4UmAv) ## What you get - **A place for every quick thought.** Memos asks nothing first: no title to invent, no folder to pick, no place to put it. Type, and the thought is kept before it goes. - **A day you can return to.** Every memo keeps the day it was written, so any day can be found again: by scrolling, by calendar, by tag, or by word. - **A record that is yours.** Your memos live where you decide, report to no one, and leave as plain Markdown whenever you like. - **Family and friends, when you choose.** A memo is yours alone until you share it. Each person writes their own memos and sees only what you choose to show. ## Quick start With Docker installed, run: ```bash docker run -d \ --name memos \ -p 5230:5230 \ -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos \ neosmemo/memos:stable ``` Open http://localhost:5230 and create the first account. Everything Memos keeps is in `~/.memos`, so back up that one folder. Other ways to run Memos, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a plain binary, are in the [deployment guide](https://usememos.com/docs/deploy). ## Upgrading Releases are tagged `YY.MM.N`, with release candidates as `YY.MM.N-rc.K` and no `v` prefix. The Docker tag `stable` follows stable releases, a month tag such as `26.10` follows the newest stable release of that month, and `canary` follows development builds. Coming from a release before v0.31.0, run [v0.31.0](https://github.com/usememos/memos/releases/tag/v0.31.0) once first; see the [upgrade requirements](store/migration/README.md). ## Around Memos - [Web Clipper](https://usememos.com/web-clipper) for [Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/memos-web-clipper/nebaoebnljalfegiidibihhkebeiklbl) and [Firefox](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/memos-web-clipper/) saves pages, selections, and images to your memos as Markdown with a link to the source. - [Memogram](https://github.com/usememos/telegram-integration) is a Telegram bot that saves your messages and images to Memos. - The [API](https://usememos.com/docs/api/latest) and [MCP server](https://usememos.com/docs/integrations/mcp) connect Memos to your own scripts and AI tools. ## Sponsors

      

Sponsor Memos through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/usememos). ## Help and contributing Questions go to the [docs](https://usememos.com/docs), [Discord](https://discord.gg/tfPJa4UmAv), or [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/usememos/memos/discussions). Bugs and ideas go to [issues](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/new/choose). Code changes start with the [contributing guide](https://usememos.com/docs/development/contributing). ## Star History

## License Memos is open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
readmeHtml:
✨ Featured sponsor: CodeRabbit — Industry-leading AI code reviews.

Seconds to write. Yours to keep.

Memos is a place for every quick thought. No title, no folder, nothing to pick: type, and the thought is kept on the day you wrote it. Your memos stay where you decide, yours alone until you share one with family and friends.

Demo · Install · Docs · Discord

What you get

  • A place for every quick thought. Memos asks nothing first: no title to invent, no folder to pick, no place to put it. Type, and the thought is kept before it goes.
  • A day you can return to. Every memo keeps the day it was written, so any day can be found again: by scrolling, by calendar, by tag, or by word.
  • A record that is yours. Your memos live where you decide, report to no one, and leave as plain Markdown whenever you like.
  • Family and friends, when you choose. A memo is yours alone until you share it. Each person writes their own memos and sees only what you choose to show.

Quick start

With Docker installed, run:

docker run -d \
  --name memos \
  -p 5230:5230 \
  -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos \
  neosmemo/memos:stable

Open http://localhost:5230 and create the first account. Everything Memos keeps is in ~/.memos, so back up that one folder.

Other ways to run Memos, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a plain binary, are in the deployment guide.

Upgrading

Releases are tagged YY.MM.N, with release candidates as YY.MM.N-rc.K and no v prefix. The Docker tag stable follows stable releases, a month tag such as 26.10 follows the newest stable release of that month, and canary follows development builds. Coming from a release before v0.31.0, run v0.31.0 once first; see the upgrade requirements.

Around Memos

  • Web Clipper for Chrome and Firefox saves pages, selections, and images to your memos as Markdown with a link to the source.
  • Memogram is a Telegram bot that saves your messages and images to Memos.
  • The API and MCP server connect Memos to your own scripts and AI tools.

Sponsors

      

Sponsor Memos through GitHub Sponsors.

Help and contributing

Questions go to the docs, Discord, or GitHub Discussions. Bugs and ideas go to issues. Code changes start with the contributing guide.

Star History

License

Memos is open source under the MIT License.

releases.name: 26.10-rc.1
releases.body:
Memos 26.10-rc.1 adds contextual editor suggestions, transcription for existing audio attachments, and a unified way to browse by creator and Space. Markdown, Calendar and Map views, image previews, and navigation receive improvements throughout the app.

### What's new

* **Editor suggestions:** New memo drafts offer tags, checklist formatting, and visibility choices based on the current filters or selected View. Suggestions are optional and disappear once fulfilled. ([#6367](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6367))
* **Audio transcription:** Transcribe an existing audio attachment from the memo editor using the configured transcription provider. The transcript is inserted into the draft for review and saving; existing text and the original audio are preserved. ([#6375](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6375))
* **Browsing:** Keep the selected creator and Space while switching between Timeline, Calendar, Map, and Attachments. The attachment library includes files from memos you can read and shows their uploaders. ([#6378](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6378))

releases.name: v0.31.0
releases.body:
Memos 0.31 adds Spaces for collaboration, Calendar and Map views for browsing your notes, and tools to move your memos between instances. Writing, search, attachments, and navigation also receive improvements throughout the app.

## Highlights

* **Spaces:** Organize memos in shared Spaces, invite people through their inbox, move memos between Spaces, and choose custom icons or emoji. Space-only visibility limits a memo's audience to active Space members, with the administrator access described below. ([#6228](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6228), [#6266](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6266), [#6285](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6285), [#6287](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6287))
* **Calendar and Map:** Browse memos by month, open a day to read or add notes for that date, and explore memos with location data on a dedicated map. releases.body:
### What's new

* **Calendar:** Browse memos by month, open a day to read its entries, and add a memo for that date. ([#6277](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6277))
* **Map:** Explore memos with location data on a dedicated map page. ([bc89ec0](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/bc89ec00060623cff52eacbc2c3ca82038e5c924))

([#6285](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6285), [#6266](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6266), [#6287](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6287))

([#6305](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6305), [#6267](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6267), [#6276](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6276))

releases.name: v0.31.0-rc.1
releases.body:
## Summary

Memos 0.31.0-rc.1 introduces first-class Spaces for collaboration while preserving individual memo ownership. It also brings a unified sidebar and global composer, inline attachment images and optional media metadata, Saved Views, richer link previews, and consistent tag and mention parsing.

This release candidate separates instance access policy from its public URL and strengthens attachment authorization, database upgrades, and live-update performance. Existing memos keep their identity, author, visibility, and relations and start as Unassigned rather than being placed into a generated default Space.

## ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* **Saved Views:** Saved Views replace Shortcuts throughout the API, MCP surface, persisted settings, resource names, and web routes. `ShortcutService` and `/api/v1/users/*/shortcuts/*` become `MemoViewService` and `/api/v1/users/*/views/*`, and the web route moves from `/shortcuts` to `/views`. Stored shortcut data is migrated automatically, but API clients, MCP integrations, and saved links must be updated. ([#6167](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/6167))
* **Memo ownership:** Instance administrators are no longer implicit memo

releases.name: v0.30.0
releases.body:
Memos 0.30 refreshes how you capture, write, and browse your notes. It introduces the Memos Web Clipper, a rebuilt Markdown editor, richer memo detail views, flexible multi-column feeds, faster rendering, and stronger authentication and sharing boundaries.

## Introducing Memos Web Clipper

Save page details, selected text, and images directly to Memos from Chromium-based browsers and Firefox. The clipper converts links, lists, code, and tables to Markdown, uploads images as attachments, and lets you review and edit every clip before saving.

Choose Private, Protected, or Public visibility, customize the output with local templates, or save selected text and images as private memos from the browser context menu. Connect through usememos.com, or connect directly with your Memos instance URL and a personal access token.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, self-hosted note-taking application designed for quick capture and Markdown support.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Memos is a self-hosted note-taking application built around a timeline-first interface to facilitate rapid thought capture. It prioritizes data ownership by allowing users to deploy the application on their own infrastructure, ensuring no telemetry or external data collection occurs. The tool natively supports Markdown for formatting and offers a lightweight footprint, available as a single Go binary or a Docker container. It provides flexibility by supporting multiple database backends, including SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, and offers REST and gRPC APIs for custom integrations. This creates a secure, highly personal knowledge base alternative to cloud services.
keyFeatures: Timeline-First Interface: Provide a simple, feed-like view for capturing and reviewing notes quickly without complex categorization overhead.
Data Ownership: Ensure complete privacy by running entirely on self-hosted infrastructure with absolutely no telemetry.
Flexible Deployment: Run as a single Go binary or a Docker container, supporting SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL for data storage.
Markdown Native: Natively support Markdown syntax for formatting notes, ensuring compatibility and ease of use.
API Integrations: Expose both REST and gRPC APIs, allowing developers to build custom tools and integrations on top of the platform.
Lightweight Architecture: Design to consume minimal system resources, making it suitable for low-power personal servers and homelabs.

useCases.title: Personal Knowledge Management
useCases.description: Individuals use the timeline interface to rapidly capture daily thoughts, links, and ideas without worrying about folder structures.

useCases.title: Private Journaling
useCases.description: Privacy-conscious users host the application locally to maintain a secure, private digital journal that cannot be accessed by third parties.

useCases.title: Custom Tool Integration
useCases.description: Developers utilize the exposed REST APIs to build automated note-taking workflows or custom frontend clients.

useCases.title: Low-Resource Deployment
useCases.description: Homelabbers deploy the lightweight Docker image alongside SQLite on a Raspberry Pi for a highly efficient note-taking solution.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Memos is designed for individuals, developers, and privacy advocates who want a fast, self-hosted alternative to cloud-based note-taking apps. Users should be comfortable with basic deployment methods like Docker or running standalone binaries.
